cfg.h.account.plan: Chooses the quotas read from quotas.json. Public repositories cost no Actions minutes on any plan. Unknown = no quota figures are shown.
cfg.h.act.allow_symlinks: Off = a repository folder that is a symbolic link is refused, so act only reads workflows inside the workspace. On = the link is followed (the workflow file must still sit inside that clone).
cfg.h.act.allowed: Entries repository:file.yml:event, all three exact (for example my-repo:ci.yml:push). Anything not listed is refused.
cfg.h.act.enabled: Off = the act command is only shown. On = a button runs it after you confirm each run; without real secrets.
cfg.h.act.timeout_seconds: The run is stopped when it takes longer.
cfg.h.ai.actions.allowed: From the closed list: rerun_failed, rerun, close_issue, act_local; one per line.
cfg.h.ai.actions.enabled: The answer may contain commands of the closed list; the page shows them and runs nothing.
cfg.h.ai.actions.execute: Adds a confirm button per action; it runs only after you accept the full command. Off by default.
cfg.h.ai.actions.max_per_hour: Most actions that may run in an hour.
cfg.h.ai.actions.ttl_seconds: A proposal can only be confirmed for this long.
cfg.h.ai.allowed_repos: Empty = every repository the monitor watches; or list the allowed ones.
cfg.h.ai.answer_language: Empty = the language of the page.
cfg.h.ai.api_key_env: Name of the environment variable that holds the key; the key itself is never saved.
cfg.h.ai.base_url: https address of an OpenAI-compatible service.
cfg.h.ai.daily_limit: Most calls to the service per day; 0 means none.
cfg.h.ai.events: build, codeql, report: one per line.
cfg.h.ai.max_input_chars: Most characters of data sent to the model.
cfg.h.ai.max_output_chars: The answer is cut at this length.
cfg.h.ai.model: Name of the model to ask.
cfg.h.ai.ollama_url: Address of the Ollama service on this computer.
cfg.h.ai.provider: none is off; an outside service receives data from your repositories.
cfg.h.ai.timeout_seconds: Seconds to wait for the model before giving up.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.brief_max_bytes: ALERTS_BRIEF.md never exceeds this many bytes (2048 by default).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.cascade.enabled: On = an alert that is red because another repository is red (its log names it, or a rule in ai_alerts.cascade.map) is listed under that one in the brief.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.block_on_sto: Off. On = at the end of a turn with real alerts open the AI is asked once to look at them (not more than once per cooldown).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.cooldown_min: Shortest time between two requests at the end of a turn.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.enabled: On = the script installed with monitor_cli.py ai-hook install adds the brief to the AI session when real alerts are open.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.max_chars: Upper limit of the text the gate script adds.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.max_lines: Lines of the brief the gate script puts in the AI session.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.client_hook.stale_hours: The gate script warns the AI when the brief is older than this many hours (the monitor may be stopped).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.enabled: Off. On = for a new red run the monitor reads its job list and the end of its log from GitHub (read only calls, counted in your allowance) and puts the failing step and about ten relevant lines in the feed.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.log_lines: How many relevant lines of the log go into each alert (10 by default).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.max_bytes: A diagnosis never exceeds this many bytes once cleaned of secrets.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.diagnose.max_per_cycle: Upper limit of runs read per cycle; the rest wait for the next one.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.enabled: Local files only (ai_alerts.jsonl and ALERTS_BRIEF.md); no network. An AI reads the brief when it starts.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.folder: Empty = next to the monitor. Choose a folder your AI sessions read.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.heartbeat.enabled: On = a small local file records the last read (stream, MCP server, gate script, endpoint) and the bottom bar shows it.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.heartbeat.window_minutes: Minutes after the last read during which the bottom bar says an AI is connected.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.hook.enabled: Off. On = a POST with a closed list of cleaned fields to the local address below.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.hook.max_per_hour: Upper limit; more alerts wait in the feed.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.stream.enabled: Off. On = GET /api/ai/stream sends the alerts as events (read only; in the network mode with the access token).
cfg.h.ai_alerts.stream.max_clients: More listeners than this get a 'too many' answer.
cfg.h.ai_alerts.stream.max_seconds: A stream ends after this time; the AI tool reconnects.
cfg.h.airgapped: On = no request leaves for the update check (it is turned off). The GitHub data you asked for are still read through gh.
cfg.h.alerts.mute_hours: How long an alert, a rule or a sentinel stays silenced when you silence it from the Alerts tab (1 to 720).
cfg.h.analytics.enabled: Durations, queue time, steps and flaky workflows.
cfg.h.analytics.flaky: Labels a workflow that failed and then passed on the same commit; it never changes what counts as red.
cfg.h.analytics.jobs_per_cycle: Completed runs whose jobs are read each cycle; 0 reads none.
cfg.h.analytics.keep_days: Days of daily figures kept for the trend.
cfg.h.analytics.max_samples: Samples kept per workflow (the oldest are dropped).
cfg.h.analytics.min_samples: A workflow shows figures only with this many samples.
cfg.h.analytics.slow_factor: A workflow is flagged when its p50 is this many times its usual one.
cfg.h.analytics.steps: Also keep the duration of each step of the jobs.
cfg.h.audit_dir: Folder where the daily reports and the audit files are.
cfg.h.cache.etag.enabled: A read that did not change answers 304 and costs no quota.
cfg.h.cache.etag.ttl_hours: After this long an endpoint is read again in full.
cfg.h.channel_on: Switches this channel on or off.
cfg.h.check_on: Switches this check on or off.
cfg.h.cold_refresh_seconds: Time between two reads of the cold repositories.
cfg.h.cold_runs_per_repo: Runs read for each cold repository.
cfg.h.discover_limit: Most repositories listed for the account (raise it for hundreds or thousands).
cfg.h.discover_refresh_seconds: Time between two searches for new repositories.
cfg.h.discovery.auto_frequency: Quiet accounts are read less often and busy ones more often, always inside the call budget. Your own intervals are the base. Off by default.
cfg.h.discovery.events: Compares the list of the account at each listing; the first look after a start is not news.
cfg.h.discovery.hide: One per line: fork, empty, private. Archived repositories are always left out.
cfg.h.discovery.suggest_groups: When three or more share a prefix. A group is only added after you confirm, and the file is copied first.
cfg.h.dispatch.required_ci: Workflow file names (for example ci.yml). A commit counts as green only when each of them succeeded on it; the default is ci.yml. Lists per repository: dispatch.required_ci_repos in the file.
cfg.h.display.blink_red_tiles: The tiles at the top (and the items of the bar at the foot) that turn red blink softly until the cause is solved. With reduced motion in the system they show a fixed thicker red edge instead.
cfg.h.display.timezone: Zone of the times written for people (log, reports, command line, notifications): local = this computer, utc, or a name such as Europe/Madrid. Machine fields stay in UTC.
cfg.h.ecosystems: Only the repositories of these ecosystems are watched (with repositories = all).
cfg.h.ecosystems_file: JSON file that names your ecosystems and their repository prefixes.
cfg.h.exclude: Repositories never watched, one name per line.
cfg.h.finops.jobs_per_cycle: 0 = the system of every job is assumed (Settings > Basic). More = the labels of each job are read for the right multiplier (Linux, Windows, macOS, larger runners), one call per run.
cfg.h.github_actions.allowed: Names: rerun_failed, rerun_run, rerun_job, cancel, close_issue, close_pr, merge_pr. By default only rerun_failed and cancel.
cfg.h.github_actions.enabled: Off = the monitor only reads. On = buttons to run again, cancel, close or merge; each action shows exactly what will be sent and asks you to confirm it.
cfg.h.github_actions.merge_method: Used by merge_pr: squash, merge or rebase.
cfg.h.github_owner: Account whose repositories are watched; empty uses the account of gh.
cfg.h.github_token.enabled: Off = the monitor uses your own gh login. On = a token you paste in Advanced is kept in the secure store of the system (never in a file of settings or a log).
cfg.h.github_token.store: auto = the system store (Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service) and a file with permissions 600 only when it is missing; system or file force one.
cfg.h.hot_hours: A repository stays hot this long after its last push or run.
cfg.h.issues_refresh_seconds: Time between two reads of the open build issues.
cfg.h.language: Language of the page, the reports and the tools; empty follows the system.
cfg.h.lint.enabled: Reads the workflow files of your local clones; nothing is sent anywhere.
cfg.h.lint.ignore: repository:file:rule, with * for any, one per line (for example demo-*:ci.yml:secrets_in_clear).
cfg.h.lint.in_report: Adds one line to the daily report when there are findings.
cfg.h.lint.refresh_seconds: Time between two scans of the clones.
cfg.h.listen.allowed_hosts: Host names or addresses accepted in the Host header, besides this computer's own (protects against DNS rebinding).
cfg.h.listen.host: A private address of this computer or 0.0.0.0 (every interface). A public address is refused.
cfg.h.listen.max_failed_attempts: After this many wrong tokens within a minute, that address is refused for five minutes.
cfg.h.listen.network: Off = only 127.0.0.1. On = also the address below, with an access token for every request and a warning in the page. Needs a restart. Warning: without HTTPS the token and the data travel unencrypted; set a certificate (listen.tls_cert_file) or an HTTPS proxy before you use it. First steps: turn listen.query_access off, and use HTTPS or a VPN.
cfg.h.listen.proxy_public_host: For an HTTPS proxy on the default port (443) that forwards Host and Origin without a port: the one host name to accept as it is. Empty = none. It only counts when HTTPS is on (direct, or with the access cookie marked Secure). Never an address with a port, a path or a user.
cfg.h.listen.query_access: Deprecated. The ?access= address opens the session once, but the token stays in the history, the logs and the Referer. Turn it off to open the session only with POST /api/access (the token in the body) or the header.
cfg.h.listen.secure_cookie: Turn on when an HTTPS proxy sits in front of the monitor (direct HTTPS marks it on its own). The token does not replace encryption: on a network you do not control, use HTTPS.
cfg.h.listen.tls_cert_file: Optional. With the key below, the monitor serves HTTPS itself using YOUR certificate (TLS 1.2 or newer). If the files cannot be used the monitor does not start. Needs a restart.
cfg.h.listen.tls_key_file: The key that goes with the certificate. Keep it outside the monitor folder; it is never shown or copied.
cfg.h.listen.token_env: The NAME of the variable (16 characters or more in its value). Without it a random token is made at each start and shown once in the console.
cfg.h.max_workers: Requests to GitHub made at the same time.
cfg.h.min_rate_remaining: Below this allowance the monitor slows down to leave quota to you.
cfg.h.mirror.enabled: Off = nothing is downloaded. On = the artifacts of finished runs are copied into the folder below, within the size ceiling.
cfg.h.mirror.folder: A folder on this computer (never a network path, never the D: drive).
cfg.h.mirror.keep_days: Copies older than this are deleted.
cfg.h.mirror.max_mb: Total size of the folder; the oldest copies are deleted first.
cfg.h.mirror.max_per_cycle: Limits the downloads (and the API calls) of each cycle.
cfg.h.mode: Full reads every run list; lite reads fewer runs to save API calls.
cfg.h.network.use_proxy: Off = outgoing notifications ignore http_proxy and https_proxy. On = they use them, and the destination (and every redirect) is checked before the proxy gets the request.
cfg.h.notify.allow_private_targets: Off = a destination that is, or resolves to, this computer or the local network (127.x, 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x with the cloud metadata address, ::1, fc00::/7) is refused, also after a redirect. On = a Matrix server in your own network is allowed.
cfg.h.notify.enabled: Nothing leaves this computer until this is on and a channel is on.
cfg.h.notify.events: red_new, stuck_new, pending_sign, offline, online, workflow_failed...; one per line.
cfg.h.notify.max_per_hour: At most this many messages leave the computer in an hour.
cfg.h.open_browser: Off = the page is only served; open the address printed on the console.
cfg.h.organizations.discover: Off = only your account is looked at. On = the organisations you belong to are listed in Basic so you can choose what to watch (one read a day).
cfg.h.otlp.enabled: Off = nothing is sent. On = traces and metrics of the runs go to the collector below.
cfg.h.otlp.endpoint: HTTPS anywhere, or plain HTTP only on this computer (for example http://127.0.0.1:4318). The OTLP/HTTP JSON protocol.
cfg.h.otlp.interval_seconds: Each export sends only the runs not sent before.
cfg.h.outputs.dashboard.enabled: Serves the ci_red document for a status dashboard on 127.0.0.1.
cfg.h.outputs.json.enabled: Serves the tables for Grafana's JSON data source on 127.0.0.1.
cfg.h.outputs.prometheus.enabled: Serves /metrics on 127.0.0.1 only; no token, no API quota.
cfg.h.outputs.prometheus.per_repo: Adds one series per repository and workflow; more series, more detail.
cfg.h.p.chat_id: Numeric id of the chat that receives the messages.
cfg.h.p.days: Age or window in days for this check.
cfg.h.p.homeserver: https address of your Matrix server.
cfg.h.p.local_url: http address on this computer that receives a POST of the event.
cfg.h.p.max_mb: Total size of live artifacts above which it is reported.
cfg.h.p.max_per_tick: Most items examined in one cycle.
cfg.h.p.minutes: Minutes a run waits before it counts as stuck.
cfg.h.p.recent_days: Only releases newer than this are checked.
cfg.h.p.retention_days: Retention in days above which an artifact is reported.
cfg.h.p.room: Internal id of the room, starting with !.
cfg.h.p.severity: info, warn or bad: how the finding is shown and counted.
cfg.h.p.token_env: NAME of the environment variable that holds the token; the token is never saved.
cfg.h.p.topic: MQTT topic that receives the events (for lights and beacons).
cfg.h.p.url_env: NAME of the environment variable that holds the webhook URL; the URL is never saved.
cfg.h.profiles_file: JSON file with the batch profiles.
cfg.h.quota.alert_percent: The second, stronger warning of the month.
cfg.h.quota.billing_api: Read only, off by default. It needs a login with permission to see billing; on a 403 or 404 the monitor keeps the estimate and says so.
cfg.h.quota.default_runner: Linux counts 1x, Windows and macOS count more (the rates are in quotas.json). Only an estimate: the runner of each job is not always known.
cfg.h.quota.warn_percent: Said once per month, through the notifications. Only for private repositories.
cfg.h.refresh_seconds: Time between two reads of the hot repositories.
cfg.h.report_history_days: How many daily reports are kept for the yesterday-versus-today view.
cfg.h.repos: all discovers the repositories of the account; or list the names to watch.
cfg.h.rule_on: Switches this rule on or off.
cfg.h.runners.enabled: Off = not read. On = idle, busy or offline for each runner of the account (one extra read per cycle).
cfg.h.runners.scope: owner = the runners of the account or organisation; repos = those of each watched repository (more calls).
cfg.h.runs_per_repo: Runs read for each hot repository.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_full_sample_unknown: Show unknown instead of green when an old workflow may be hidden beyond the sample.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_resolve_max_calls_per_: Extra lookups per cycle to settle an unknown workflow; 0 never asks.
cfg.h.sentinel.a2_resolve_ttl_seconds: How long an answer of that lookup is kept.
cfg.h.sentinel.alerts_hot_seconds: Time between two reads of the security alerts of hot repositories.
cfg.h.sentinel.audit_files.reconciliatio: Name pattern of the reconciliation files in the audit folder.
cfg.h.sentinel.audit_files.rounds: Name pattern of the rounds files.
cfg.h.sentinel.audit_files.rounds_extra: Name pattern of the extra rounds files.
cfg.h.sentinel.budget_per_hour: Most API calls the sentinel makes in an hour.
cfg.h.sentinel.candidate_days: Days with unpublished changes before a repository is a release candidate.
cfg.h.sentinel.candidate_min_entries: Changelog entries needed to be a candidate.
cfg.h.sentinel.ci_red_audit_copy: Also copies ci_red.json into the audit folder.
cfg.h.sentinel.ci_red_file: Where ci_red.json is written; empty is next to the monitor, off writes none.
cfg.h.sentinel.enabled: Switches the whole sentinel (alerts, releases, readiness) on or off.
cfg.h.sentinel.hot_hours: A repository is hot for the sentinel this long after a push.
cfg.h.sentinel.hygiene_seconds: Time between two checks of repository rules, labels and files.
cfg.h.sentinel.max_calls_per_tick: Most API calls the sentinel makes in one cycle.
cfg.h.sentinel.min_rate_remaining: Below this allowance the sentinel waits.
cfg.h.sentinel.minutes_budget: Ceiling of Actions minutes per ecosystem; empty means no ceiling.
cfg.h.sentinel.minutes_budget_period: Window over which the minutes of each ecosystem are counted.
cfg.h.sentinel.pending_sign_hours: A green build waiting this long for its signature is reported.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.enabled: Switches release readiness, ecosystem health and pins on or off.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.min_coverage: An ecosystem gets a score only when this share of its repositories has data.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.pins.max_depth: Folder levels searched for lock files.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.pins.refresh_se: Time between two readings of the pinned versions.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.pins.sources: Where the pins live, as a JSON list; empty reads nothing.
cfg.h.sentinel.readiness.warn_below: The report warns about an ecosystem whose score is below this.
cfg.h.sentinel.require_verified_signatur: A signature counts only when it verifies against the public key of the ecosystem.
cfg.h.sentinel.required_files: Files every repository must have; one group per line, alternatives separated by ;.
cfg.h.sentinel.skip_candidate_prefixes: Repositories starting with these prefixes are never proposed for a release.
cfg.h.sentinel.stale_pr_days: A pull request open this long is reported as stale.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.budget_share: Share of the sentinel budget these checks may use.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.enabled: Switches all the checks of the Actions and releases surface on or off.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.local_seconds: Time between two scans of the local clones.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.max_repos_per_tic: Repositories read from GitHub in one cycle.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.min_rate_factor: Starts only when the allowance left is this many times the pause limit.
cfg.h.sentinel.surface.refresh_seconds: Time between two readings of GitHub data of each repository.
cfg.h.sentinel.workers: Requests the sentinel makes at the same time.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.enabled: Switches the sentinel of issues and pull requests on or off (off by default).
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.max_repos_per_tic: How many repositories one round reads (two requests each): the rest wait for the next round.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.min_rate_remainin: The sentinel stops while the GitHub allowance is below this.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.refresh_seconds: Time between two rounds of the Collab sentinel.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.repos: all, or a list of repositories, or the ecosystems to watch.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.ignore_labe: An issue or pull request with one of these labels (put by a person on GitHub) raises no alert; one per line.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.issue_criti: An open issue with one of these labels is always flagged; one per line.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.issue_stale: An open issue with no activity for this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.pr_conflict: A pull request with conflicts for this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.pr_draft_ma: A draft pull request open for this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.pr_review_p: A pull request with a requested review that has waited this long is flagged.
cfg.h.sentinels.collab.rules.watch_exter: Also flags issues from people outside the team that nobody has answered after a day.
cfg.h.session_guard: The page asks for a fresh token right before it saves a setting or confirms an action, so another page in your browser cannot do it for you.
cfg.h.show_unclassified: Repositories that no ecosystem claims appear in an automatic group Unclassified instead of disappearing (only with all ecosystems).
cfg.h.signed_dir: Folder with the local records of signing and batches.
cfg.h.sound.cooldown_seconds: Minimum time between two sounds, so a burst of failures sounds once. 0 = no pause.
cfg.h.sound.enabled: Main switch of the "bing bing" (two short tones) of the page. The chip "Sound" of the bar at the foot mutes it in this browser.
cfg.h.sound.on_connection_lost: Sounds once when the connection to GitHub goes from online to offline.
cfg.h.sound.on_new_red: Sounds when a failure that was not there before appears (not for the ones already open and not at every refresh).
cfg.h.sound.server_beep: Off by default. The monitor itself sounds two tones on this computer (Windows beep, macOS Glass sound, Linux canberra or the terminal bell) for a new red or a lost connection when no page is open. It never uses the network and a missing program is not an error.
cfg.h.sound.volume: Volume of the tones of the page, from 1 to 100 (moderate by default). Use the button "Test sound" in This browser to hear it.
cfg.h.stuck_minutes: A run that lasts longer than this is shown as stuck.
cfg.h.targets_file: JSON file with the catalogue of build targets.
cfg.h.tools_dir: Folder of your local signing tools; empty if you have none.
cfg.h.tui.refresh_seconds: Time between two redraws of the terminal view.
cfg.h.updates.check: One read-only request a day to the public releases page, through your own gh. It never downloads or installs anything and sends nothing about you.
cfg.h.webhook.enabled: Opens the receiver on 127.0.0.1; every request needs a valid signature.
cfg.h.webhook.live_events_keep: The newest events held in memory.
cfg.h.webhook.max_per_minute: Per minute. More are answered but ignored.
cfg.h.webhook.record_events: Use workflow_run and workflow_job events to update the runs without reading GitHub.
cfg.h.webhook.replay_seconds: A delivery that was already accepted is refused again during this time (protection against a captured request sent twice).
cfg.h.webhook.signing_state: Whether the secret in the file is defined; it is never shown here.
cfg.h.weight: Points taken off the health score of an ecosystem for each case.
cfg.h.workspace_root: Folder that holds your local clones.

doctor.f.backend: The plain file (permissions 600) is the weakest store: a backup of your home folder copies it. Prefer the store of the system (set github_token.store to system) or keep using your own gh login.
doctor.f.credential: Two or more accounts read GitHub with the same personal access token (the detail shows a short fingerprint and the accounts, never the token): one rate limit and one point of failure for all of them, and a leak exposes every account. Give each account its own token.
doctor.f.degraded: Some parts failed and the monitor kept running without them (the number and the origin are shown). Look at the log; if the number keeps growing, restart and report it.
doctor.f.docker: Not needed unless you want the container example.

doctor.f.folder: Move the monitor to a folder where you can write.
doctor.f.gh: Install gh with one of these commands.
doctor.f.login: Log in once with gh. The monitor keeps no token unless you switch that on in Advanced.
doctor.f.network: GitHub cannot be reached; check the connection or the proxy.
doctor.f.port: Both ports are busy; start with another one.
doctor.f.python: Install a newer Python from python.org.
doctor.f.quota: The allowance is low or unreadable; wait for it to renew.
doctor.f.risks: network_all = listening on every interface (use one private address); execute_network = AI actions may run while the monitor is reachable from the network; token_file = the own token sits in a plain file; act_network = act can run while the monitor is reachable from the network. Turn one of the two options off.
doctor.f.targets: Only the neutral example is used; create your own copies.
doctor.f.textual: Only for the interactive terminal application.
doctor.f.timezone: The zone is not recognised on this computer, so the times are shown in UTC. Use "local", "utc" or an IANA name such as Europe/Madrid in Settings (Interface), or fix MONITOR_TIMEZONE.
doctor.f.token: Turn session_guard back on in the settings.
